key_insight: Multi-omics and machine learning identified JAK–STAT signaling as a convergent feature of immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis, with amplified inflammatory programs in CHIP carriers.
clinical_relevance: These findings nominate cytokine-guided risk stratification and JAK–STAT-directed treatment as research strategies for this potentially fatal cancer-immunotherapy complication.
method: Machine learning and explainable AI analyzed cytokine profiles from ICI-treated patients.
Single-cell multi-omics mapped immune-cell contributions and inflammatory pathways across three cohorts.
Stanford CyTOF data provided validation of Yale proteomic analyses.
evidence_signal: The study enrolled 236 cardio-oncology patients, including 88 receiving ICI, and analyzed single-cell data from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63), finding convergent module-level JAK–STAT signals.
watch_item: The abstract reports associations, not validated clinical prediction performance or evidence that JAK–STAT-directed treatment improves outcomes.
paper_title: Cytokine Signatures of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis and the Modifying Role of Clonal Hematopoiesis: A Machine-Learning and Multi-Omics Study
